[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to Equinix. Equinix Inc was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson, both former facilities managers at Digital Equipment Corporation, per Equinix corporate history as summarized on Wikipedia, fetched this session. Equinix is headquartered in Redwood City, California, and converted to a real estate investment trust structure in January 2015, later describing itself, per Wikipedia, as a digital infrastructure company from September 2020 onward. Equinix own about page, fetched this session, states the company currently operates 281 data centers spanning metros across six continents, with more than 513,000 interconnections and more than 10,500 customers, and describes itself directly as the world digital infrastructure company. Wikipedia separately states a close but not identical figure, approximately 260 data centers across 33 countries on five continents with about 13,000 employees, as of 2025, both figures are recorded here rather than reconciled. Wikipedia own account of Equinix acquisition history lists a 2002 merger with I-STT and Pihana Pacific expanding into the Asia Pacific region, a 2007 acquisition of IXEurope that established the company European market presence, a 2015 acquisition of TelecityGroup for about 3.8 billion dollars, its largest acquisition at that time, a 2016 purchase of 29 data centers from Verizon, a 2020 acquisition of the bare metal cloud provider Packet, and a 2021 acquisition of Main One for about 320 million dollars expanding into West Africa. Equinix trades on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol EQIX. This batch covers 11 facilities in this registry that had carried an exhausted research status, all in Europe, across Finland, Italy, Spain, and Poland, the first non United States batch researched in this campaign. Given that both the 2007 IXEurope acquisition and the 2015 TelecityGroup acquisition materially built out Equinix European footprint, either or both are plausible historical origins for some of these European facilities, but no per facility lineage to either predecessor company was found on Equinix own current facility pages fetched this session, so this batch does not assert which historical company, if either, any specific building traces back to. The remaining 45 facilities attributed to Equinix in this registry, all in the United States, were already marked complete before this session and are untouched by this batch. Equinix own dedicated page for this facility, ML5, fetched this session, gives its address as Via Marisa Bellisario 5, 20019 Settimo Milanese, Italy, a short distance from the sibling ML7x facility also researched in this batch on the same street, and states 4,200 square meters, 45,208 square feet, of colocation space in a three storey reinforced concrete building. The page describes the site as strategically located next to Via Caldera, described on the page as the most well connected location in Milan. The page states N plus 1 power and cooling redundancy and a 99.9999 percent or better global uptime guarantee. The page did not publish a specific IT capacity figure in megawatts or kilowatts.
